questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why hunting safaris are becoming more popular
How to take good photos of wild animals
Whether nature and wildlife tourism helps or harms
The most famous animals in Africa
questions.why: Beth says they'll be asking: is ecotourism good or bad?

questions.q: How are safaris changing, according to Neil?
options: Tourists now shoot photos, not animals
They are becoming shorter and cheaper
They are moving from Africa to Asia
Fewer tourists are going on them each year
questions.why: Neil says safaris are swapping their guns for cameras.

questions.q: What is Vicky Smith's main point?
options: All nature tourism is good for wild animals
Swimming with dolphins is a responsible activity
Tourists should avoid travelling to Africa
Nature tourism isn't always responsible
questions.why: She says just because tourism is nature-based, it doesn't mean it's responsible or sustainable.

questions.q: Which of these does Vicky Smith give as an irresponsible activity?
options: Watching snow leopards from far away
Having selfies taken with drugged tigers
Staying with local families
Walking in national parks
questions.why: She lists tiger selfies where the tigers are drugged, as well as dolphin shows and elephant-riding.

questions.q: What are the two requirements for genuine ecotourism?
options: Low prices and comfortable, modern hotels
Taking photos and getting close to animals
Not disturbing nature; helping locals
Travelling by train and staying for a long time
questions.why: Neil says tourists should observe nature without interfering and their money should support traditional communities.

questions.q: How many wildlife tourists does Tajikistan get each year?
options: Fewer than two dozen
About two hundred
Thousands
None at all
questions.why: Antonia says Tajikistan gets less than two dozen wildlife tourists a year.

questions.q: Why does Antonia Bolingbroke-Kent mention Tajikistan?
options: As an example of a country with too many tourists
As a place where tourists can ride wild animals
As a country that has recently banned ecotourism
As ecotourism that helps animals and people
questions.why: She uses it to contrast with irresponsible tourism: animals are unaffected and local communities genuinely benefit.

questions.q: According to Antonia, how are animals like snow leopards watched in Tajikistan?
options: From helicopters
From a distance, without changing their behaviour
In special zoos
Very closely, so tourists can touch them
questions.why: She says they are observed from a distance and their behaviour is not affected.
